source.publication: 2025 Kentucky Form 740 packet with instructions (Kentucky Department of Revenue), with 2025 Form 740, Schedule M, Schedule P and Schedule ITC
source.section: Form 740 (2025) page 1 lines 5-19 and page 2 lines 20-22 (740_2025.pdf PDF pp.1-2); packet PDF p.13 Line 5, Lines 6-9 (Kentucky AGI), Line 10 'Nonitemizers, enter the standard deduction of $3,270 ... If filing a joint return, only one $3,270 standard deduction is allowed', Line 11, Line 12 'Multiply line 11 by four percent (.04)'; packet PDF p.3 'For 2025, the standard deduction is $3,270' and 'the tax rate for individual income tax is 4%'; Schedule M (2025) PDF p.1 line 9 and PDF p.3 Line 9 Pension Income Exclusion ('100 percent of taxable retirement benefits or $31,110, whichever is less ... for each taxpayer and must be computed independently of your spouse') and Pension Income Exclusion Worksheet Steps 1-3; Schedule P (2025) PDF p.1 flowchart and lines 1-4, PDF p.2 Types of Income Subject to Exclusion; packet PDF p.9 chart item 4; Schedule M (2025) PDF p.1 line 10 and PDF p.3 Line 10 (taxable Social Security from Form 1040 line 6(b) subtracted); packet PDF p.3 Social Security remains exempt; Schedule ITC (2025) PDF p.2 Section B line 1 (taxpayer) and line 5 (spouse) 'If you were 65 on or before 12/31/2025, enter 40'; Form 740 lines 16-18 (line 18: if line 17 is larger than line 16, enter zero); packet PDF p.14 Line 17; Schedule ITC (2025) PDF p.2 Section C Family Size Tax Credit Table (family size one: not over 15,650 100% ... over 20,815 0; family size two: not over 21,150 100% ... over 28,130 0); packet PDF p.26 Worksheet for Computation of Modified Gross Income lines (a)-(j) and Section C family size definitions; packet PDF p.11 Modified Gross Income; packet PDF p.14 Line 20 and Line 21 (MGI 42,760 or less); Form 740 page 2 lines 20-22 (line 21: line 19 times the decimal from Schedule ITC)

worked: Married filing jointly, both 67: one spouse's private pension is over the 31,110 limit and the other's IRA distribution is under it; each spouse computes their own exclusion. Taxable Social Security is subtracted. Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = private pension (person 0) 45,000.00 + IRA distribution (person 1) 12,000.00 + taxable Social Security 37,450.00 = 94,450.00. Federal taxable income = 94,450.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 - 2 x 1,600.00 for 65 or older = 59,750.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form 740, Filing Status 3 (married, filing joint return; incomes added in Column B). Line 5 federal AGI 94,450.00. Line 6 additions 0.00; line 7 = 94,450.00. Person 0 (Column B) Pension Income Exclusion Worksheet Step 1 line (d) = 45,000.00, more than 31,110; Step 3: no federal, Kentucky state or Kentucky local government pension and no Tier 2 railroad benefits, so 31,110 is entered: excludable 31,110.00. Person 1 (Column A) Pension Income Exclusion Worksheet Step 1 line (d) = 12,000.00, 31,110 or less, so Step 2 enters the whole: excludable 12,000.00. Schedule M line 9 excludable retirement income = 43,110.00 (joint filers combine the two separately computed amounts). Schedule M line 10 taxable Social Security from Form 1040 line 6(b) 37,450.00. Schedule M line 17 total subtractions 80,560.00; Form 740 line 8 80,560.00. Line 9 Kentucky AGI = 94,450.00 - 80,560.00 = 13,890.00. Line 10 standard deduction 3,270.00 (one deduction on a joint return); line 11 taxable income = 13,890.00 - 3,270.00 = 10,620.00. Line 12 tax = 10,620.00 x 0.04 = 424.80; lines 13 and 15 0.00; line 14 and line 16 424.80. Schedule ITC Section B: person 0 (age 67) 40, person 1 (age 67) 40; under-65 persons 0; line 17 = 80.00; line 18 = 424.80 - 80.00 = 344.80. Line 19 = 344.80. Modified gross income worksheet: (a) 94,450.00; (c) non-Kentucky municipal interest 0.00; (e) 94,450.00; (f) Kentucky AGI 13,890.00; (i) 13,890.00; (j) greater = 94,450.00. MGI 94,450.00 is over 42,760: no Family Size Tax Credit; line 21 0.00. Line 22 = 344.80 - 0.00 = 344.80. Credits = 80.00 + 0.00 = 80.00; state income tax 344.80. The form enters whole dollars; expected keeps the formula result to the cent. Federal taxable Social Security (given): provisional income = 57,000.00 + 50% x 48,000.00 = 81,000.00; 85% x (81,000.00 - 44,000.00) = 31,450.00 + lesser of 6,000.00 or 24,000.00 = 37,450.00, under 85% x 48,000.00 = 40,800.00, so 37,450.00. Both spouses had income, so Filing Status 2 (separately on a combined return) is open and would give each spouse 3,270 (6,540 in all, 130.80 less tax); this case is a joint return (Filing Status 3), where only one 3,270 is allowed, which is also what the projection applies.
accepted_approximations: One 3,270 standard deduction is applied to a married couple. On a combined return (Filing Status 2), open when both spouses had income, each spouse takes 3,270.
